The student should bear in mind that generally if the qurrāʾ recite with istifhām in the first occurrence, they will recite as ikhbār in the second occurrence, and vice versa. Occasionally, they will recite both as istifhām. However, they will never recite both as ikhbār. Once this is understood, the following lines will be simple to understand.

The author explains that Abū Jaʿfar will read as ikhbār in the first occurrence in all nine places. It is understood that if he reads as ikhbār in the first occurrence, he will read as istifhām in the second occurrence. Thereafter, he excludes two places: Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah (سِوٰى إِذَا وَقَعَتْ) and the first place in Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt (أَوَّلِ الِّذّبْحِ). In these two places Abū Jaʿfar will read with istifhām in the first occurrence and as ikhbār in the second (فَاسْأَلَا).
Predicate in the second (of the istifhām that recurs) for Yaʿqūb, except in (Sūrat) al-ʿAnkabūt; (read it) contrastingly. And in (Sūrat) al-Naml (read) istifhām in both places for Yaʿqūb.

# Commentary

Yaʿqūb will read as ikhbār in the second occurrence of the recurring istifhām in all nine places. It is understood that in the first occurrence he will read as a question (istifhām). Thereafter, two places are excluded: Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, in which he will read as ikhbār in the first occurrence and as istifhām in the second (اعْكِسَا), and in Sūrat al-Naml, in which is will read as a question (istifhām) in both occurrences.

Since no mention is made of Khalaf, he will agree with his bases and read as a question in both occurrences, the first and the second.

They will all apply their rules mentioned previously when two hamzahs appear together: Abū Jaʿfar making tashīl with idkhāl, Ruways having tashīl without idkhāl, while Rouḥ and Khalaf have taḥqīq of both hamzahs.

زَتَمْهَالْكَانِ مِنْ نِيْتَمَلِ

Two hamzahs in two words refer to two hamzat al-qaṭʿī’s that are both mutaḥarrik, appearing alongside each other in two different words. This necessitates that the first hamzah comes at the end of one word while the second comes at the start of the following word. Note that the only way they will be read together is during waṣl.

The two hamzahs in two words differ from the two hamzahs in one word in that in the latter, the first hamzah is always maftūḥah. Furthermore, with regards to two hamzahs appearing in one word, the tashīl is always made in the second hamzah; whereas if two hamzahs appear in two words, the tashīl may take place in the first or the second hamzah.

Two hamzahs coming together in 2 different words are of 2 types:

1) مُتَّفِقُ الحَرَكَة – the 2 hamzahs agree in their ḥarakāt.

2) مُخْتَلِفُ الحَرَكَة – the 2 hamzahs have different ḥarakāt.

If the two hamzahs agree in ḥarakāt then they are either both maftūḥah e.g. جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا, جَآءَ أَحَد, both maḍmūmah e.g. أَوْلِيَآءُ أُولٓئِك or both maksūrah e.g. مِنَ السَّمَآءِ إِنّ.

If two hamzahs differ in their ḥarakāt, then they are of five types:

1) The first hamzah is maftūḥah and the second maksūrah e.g. تَفِيٓءَ إِلٰىَ.

2) The first hamzah is maftūḥah and the second is maḍmūmah e.g. جٓاءَ أُمَّة.

3) The first hamzah is maḍmūmah and the second is maftūḥah e.g. نَشٓاءُ أَصَبْنَا.

4) The first hamzah is maksūrah and the second is maftūḥah e.g. مِنَ السَّمَاءِ أَوِئْتِنَا.

5) The first hamzah is maḍmūmah and the second maksūrah e.g. يَشٓاءُ إِلٰىَ.

There are no places in the Qurʾān where the first hamzah is maksūrah and the second is maḍmūmah.

In the condition that they (two hamzahs) agree, make tashīl of the second (hamzah) for Abū Jaʿfar and Ruways; apply taḥqīq of them (the two hamzahs) both, and similarly (apply taḥqīq) when they differ for Rouḥ.

# Commentary

If the two hamzahs agree then Abū Jaʿfar and Ruways will read with tashīl in the second hamzah. Abū Jaʿfar would contradict Qālūn who drops the hamzah if they are both maftūḥah, and makes tashīl of the first hamzah if they are maḍmūmah or maksūrah. Similarly, he differs from Warsh who would allow ibdāl in addition to tashīl of the second hamzah. Ruways differs from Abū ʿAmr who drops the first hamzah according to the view of the majority, while a minority maintains that he drops the second hamzah.

It is understood that when the two hamzahs differ, Abū Jaʿfar and Ruways will agree with their basis i.e. read with tashīl in numbers one and two, ibdāl into a wāw in number three, ibdāl into a yāʾ in number four and both tashīl as well as ibdāl into a wāw in number five.

If two hamzahs agree, as well as when they differ, Rouḥ will read with taḥqīq.

Since no mention is made of Khalaf, he will agree with his basis and read both hamzahs with taḥqīq.

الْهَمْزُ الْمُفْرَدُ The isolated hamzah is that which is not found next to another hamzah. It may be divided into two: the hamzah sākinah and the hamzah mutaḥarrikah. The hamzah sākinah is either the fāʾ kalimah, the ʿayn kalimah or the lām kalimah e.g. مُؤْمِنُونَ, الِّذّئْبُ, اِقْرَأ. In this chapter, takhfīf in the hamzah sākinah is via ibdāl or ibdāl with idghām. Takhfīf in the hamzah mutaḥarrikah is via ibdāl, ḥadhf, ibdāl with idghām and tashīl.
(Apply) taḥqīq (in) it’s (the hamzah’s) sākin for Yaʿqūb; and surely make ibdāl for Abū Jaʿfar, except in أَنْبِئْهْمْ and وَنَبِّئْهْمُ, then do not (make ibdāl).

# Commentary

The author starts his discussion of this chapter with the hamzah sākinah.

Yaʿqūb will read with taḥqīq in the hamzah sākinah, whether it is the the fāʾ, ʿayn or lām kalimah, contradicting al-Sūsī.[33]

Abū Jaʿfar contradicts his basis – both Qālūn and Warsh – in making ibdāl in the hamzah sākinah, whether it is the fāʾ, ʿayn or lām kalimah, except in أَنْبِئْهْمْ of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 33, and وَنَبِّئْهْمُ of Sūrat al-Ḥijr, 51 and Sūrat al-Qamar, 28.

With these two exceptions mentioned, Abū Jaʿfar will still have ibdāl in نَبِّئْنَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ and إِلَّا نَبَّأْتُكُمَا بِتَأْوِيلِهِ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 36, 37.

[33] Yaʿqūb will make ibdāl in يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ of Sūrat al-Kahf, 94 and Sūrat al-Ambiyāʾ, 96. Perhaps the author does not make mention of it here because Imam al-Shāṭibī mentions it in the farsh (inconsistent differences) of the Shāṭibiyyah, and Yaʿqūb will therefore agree with his basis. See line

And (in) وَرِئْيًا, then make it’s idghām, as (in) all of رُؤْيَا. (Apply) ibdāl (in) يُؤَيِّدْ for Ibn Jammāz and the likes of مُؤَجَّلَا… Similarly, (apply ibdāl in) قُرِئَ, اُسْتُهْزِئَ, نَاشِئَةَ, يُبَطِّيْ,)لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُم(نُبَوِّي,)رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ(رِيَا)شَانِئَكَ,)لَيُبَطِّئَنّ and خَاسِئًا for Abū Jaʿfar.

# Commentary

In أَحْسَنُ أَثٰثً وَرِءْيًا of Sūrah Maryam, 74, Abū Jaʿfar will make ibdāl of the hamzah into a yāʾ and subsequently make idghām of the yāʾ into the yāʾ i.e. وَرِيًّاً.

Similarly, in الرُّءْيَا, ibdāl of the hamzah is made into a wāw, thereafter changing the wāw into a yāʾ and subsequently making idghām of the yāʾ into the yāʾ i.e. الرُّيَّا. By جَمِيعِهِ (all of it), لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُوُنَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 43, أَفْتُونِي فِي رُءْيٰيَ of Sūrah Yūsuf, 43, 100 and رُءْيَاكَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 5 etc. are all included.[34]

In the second half of the line the author starts discussing the hamzah mutaḥarrikah. It may be divided into two: that which is preceded by a mutaḥarrik or that which is preceded by a sākin.

If preceded by a mutaḥarrik, then it is found in six different conditions:

1) Hamzah maftūḥah preceded by a ḍammah e.g. يُؤَيِّدُ, مُؤَجَّلَا.

2) Hamzah maftūḥah preceded by a kasrah e.g. قُرِئَ, اُسْتُهْزِئَ, نَاشِئَةَ, رِئَاءَ, لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُم, لَيُبَطِّئَنّ, شَانِئَكَ, خَاسِئًا, مُلِئَتْ, الخَاطِئَة, مِائَة, فِئَة, مَوْطِئًا.

3) Hamzah maḍmūmah preceded by a kasrah e.g. مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ, الْمُنْشِئُونَ.

4) Hamzah maḍmūmah preceded by a fatḥah e.g. تَطَئُوهَا, تَطَئُوهُمْ, وَلَا يَطَئُونَ.

5) Hamzah maftūḥah preceded by a fatḥah e.g. مُتَّكَئًا.

6) Hamzah maksūrah preceded by a kasrah e.g. خَاطِئِيَن, الْخَاطِئِيَن, مُتَّكِئِيَن, الْمُسْتَهْزِئِيَن.

If preceded by a sākin, then it will either be an alif, wāw, yāʾ or zāy.

Ibn al-Jazarī discusses the matters pertaining to the hamzah mufradah with this format in mind.

Ibn Jammāz will make ibdāl into a wāw in يُؤَيِّدُ of Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 13, i.e. يُوَيِّدُ. Ibn Wardān, Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will read with taḥqīq.

Abū Jaʿfar will make ibḍal into a wāw in words the likes of مُؤَجَّلَا i.e. those words in which the hamzah maftūḥah is the fāʾ kalimah and preceded by a ḍammah e.g. يُؤَلِّفُ, يُؤَدُّهُ, يُؤَاخِذُ, مُؤَذِّنٌ, وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ, يُؤَخِّرُهُم. It will therefore exclude words like الفُؤَادُ, فُؤَادَكَ, بِسُؤَالٍ and وَلُؤْلُؤًا, because though the hamzah is maftūḥah and preceded by a ḍammah, it is not the fāʾ al-kalimah. In the latter examples Abū Jaʿfar will read with taḥqīq.

From the second line, the author starts mentioning 13 words in which Abū Jaʿfar will make ibdāl into a yāʾ during waqf and waṣl. Eight are mentioned in this line: قُرِئَ of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 204 and Sūrat al-Inshiqāq, 21, اُسْتُهْزِئَ of Sūrat al-Anʿām, 10, Sūrat al-Raʿd, 32 and Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, 41, نَاشِئَةَ of Sūrat al-Muzzammil, 6, رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 264, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 38 and Sūrat al-Anfāl, 47, لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُم of Sūrat al-Naḥl, 41 and Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, 58, لَيُبَطِّئَنّ of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 72, شَانِئَكَ of Sūrat al-Kouthar, 3 and خَاسِئًا of Sūrat al-Mulk, 4.

[34] By specifying الرُّءْيَا and all it’s appearances, words like وَتُؤْوِي of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, 51, and وَتُؤْوِيهِ of Sūrat al-Maʿārij, 13, are excluded i.e. only ibdāl will take place in them, and not ibdāl with idghām.
Similarly, (ibdāl is applied in) مُلِئَتْ, الخَاطِئَة, مِائَة, فِئَة, so apply it (ibdāl) generally for him (in these words); while a choice is (found) in مَوْطِئًا for Abū Jaʿfar.

# Commentary

The remaining five words in which Abū Jaʿfar has ibdāl in, is mentioned in this line: مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًا of Sūrat al-Jinn, 8, خَاطِئَةٍ of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, 16, بِالْخَاطِئَةِ of Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 9, مِائِة, مِائَتَيْنِ, فِئَةٌ, فِئَتَيْنِ, الفِئَتَانِ, wherever they might appear.

فَأَطْلِقْ لَهُ (apply ibdāl generally for him i.e. Abū Jaʿfar) means that ibdāl will be applied unrestrictedly in the latter three words i.e. the last three words mentioned. This would include الخَاطِئَة, whether it is nakirah or maʿrifah; مِائَة and فِئَةٌ, whether they are singular or dual.

In مَوْطِئًا of Sūrat al-Toubah, 12, Abū Jaʿfar will have a choice of making either ibdāl or taḥqīq.

Omit (the hamzah in) مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ and the (entire) chapter, along with تَطَئُوهَا) تَطَوْ, خَاطِئِيَن) خَاطِيَن,(مُتَّكَئًا) مُتَّكًا,(يَطَئُونَ) يَطَوْ,(تَطَئُوهُمْ) and (مُتَّكِئِيَن) مُتَّكِئِي for Abū Jaʿfar.

# Commentary

مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ and it’s entire chapter refers to all those words in which the hamzah maḍmūmah is preceded by a kasrah e.g. أَنْبِئُونِي of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 31, مُتَّكِئُونَ of Sūrah Yāsīn, 56, لِيُوَاطِئُوا of Sūrat al-Toubah, 37 and قُلِ اسْتَهْزِءُوا of Sūrat al-Toubah,

64. Abū Jaʿfar will drop the hamzah and the letter before it will be read with a ḍammah due to the wāw i.e. مُسْتَهْزُونَ, أَنْبُونِي, مُتَّكُونَ, لِيُوَاطُوا, قُلِ اسْتَهْزُوا.

The author does not explicitly mention that the letter before the hamzah will get a ḍammah since it is well known and apparent amongst the qurrāʾ.

In three words where the hamzah maḍmūmah is preceded by a fatḥah, Abū Jaʿfar will drop the hamzah while the letter before it will retain its fatḥah: تَطَئُوهَا of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, 27, أَنْ تَطَئُوهُمْ of Sūrat al-Fatḥ, 25, and وَلَا يَطَئُونَ of Sūrat al-Toubah, 120 i.e. تَطَوْهَا, تَطَوْهُم and يَطَوْنَ.

Abū Jaʿfar will also drop the hamzah in وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنّ مُتَّكَئًا of Sūrah Yūsuf, 31, in which the hamzah maftūḥah is preceded by a fatḥah i.e. مُتَّكًا.

In three words, Abū Jaʿfar will drop the hamzah when it is maksūrah and preceded by a kasrah: خَاطِئِيَن, whether it is nakirah e.g. إِنَّا كُنَّا خَاطِئِيَن of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 97, or maʿrifah e.g. إِنَّكِ كُنْتِ مِنَ الْخَاطِئِيَن of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 29, as well as in مُتَّكِئِيَن of Sūrat al-Raḥmān, 54 and 76. The third word is mentioned at the start of the next line.
As (well as apply ḥadhf in) مُسْتَهْزِئِيَن, with a choice (of ḥadhf in) (الْمُنْشِئُونَ) مُنْشُونَ for Ibn Wardān. Make idghām in جُزْءًا, كَهَيْئَة and النَّسِيِءُ; then (apply) tashīl (in)…

# Commentary

The third word in which Abū Jaʿfar will drop the hamzah is الْمُسْتَهْزِئِيَن.[35] Since the ḥadhf in the hamzah maksūrah preceded by a kasrah is restricted to these three words, others like خَاسِئِيَن are excluded and will therefore be read with taḥqīq.[36]

In أَمْ نَحْنُ الْمُنْشِئُونَ of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah, 72, Ibn Wardān will have a choice of dropping the hamzah or reading it. Ibn Jammāz will drop the hamzah according to the precept outlined in line 32 regarding مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ.

35 الْمُسْتَهْزِئِيَن only comes one place in the Qurʾān: إِنَّا كَفَيْنَاكَ الْمُسْتَهْزِئِيَن of Sūrat al-Ḥijr, 95. Though the author mentions مُسْتَهْزِئِيَن in the poem, it does not appear in the Qurʾān as nakirah.

Thereafter, Ibn al-Jazarī starts discussing the hamzah mutaḥarrikah preceded by a sākin.

Abū Jaʿfar will make idghām in: مِنْهُنّ جُزْءًا of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 260, جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ of Sūrat al-Ḥijr, 44 and مِنْ عِبَادِهِ جُزْءًا of Sūrat al-Zukhruf, 15. Abū Jaʿfar changes the hamzah to a zāy, and makes idghām of one zāy into the other i.e. جُزًّا and جُزّ.

Abū Jaʿfar will also make idghām in كَهَيْئَة الطَّيْرْ of Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 49 and Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 110, as well as in إِنَّمَا النَّسِيِٓءُ زِيَادَةٌ of Sūrat al-Toubah, 37.

At the end of the line, the author indicates that Abū Jaʿfar will make tashīl. The words in which he makes tashīl is mentioned in the next line.

[36] See al-Taḥbīr, pg 60. Abū Jaʿfar will make ḥadhf in الصَّابِئِيَن, agreeing with his basis, Nāfiʿ. Similarly, he will agree with his basis and make ḥadhf in الصَّابِئُونَ.

(Apply) tashīl (in) أَرَيْتَ, إِسْرَائِيلَ and كَائِنْ while making madd (in the latter) for Abū Jaʿfar; with (tashīl in) اللَّاءِ and هٰأَنْتُم (for Abū Jaʿfar), while Yaʿqūb makes taḥqīq in them both (the last two words).

# Commentary

Abū Jaʿfar will make tashīl in five words mentioned in this line. The first is in أَرَءَيْتَ in all its forms e.g. أَرَءَيْتَكُم, أَرَءَيْتَكَ, أَرَءَيْتُم, أَفَرَءَيْتُم, أَفَرَءَيْتَ etc. Here he differs with Warsh who would have ibdāl in addition to tashīl.

The second word is إِسْرَآئِيلَ wherever it comes. Abū Jaʿfar will make tashīl in the second hamzah. Due to a change taking place in the cause of the madd (sabab al-madd), both qaṣr and madd may be read. This is explained by Imam al-Shāṭibī in the following line:

وَإِنْ حَرْفُ مَدقَبْلَ هَمْزٍ مُغَيٍّر يَ * جُزْ قَصْرْهُ وَالْمَدُ مَا زَالَ أَعْدَلَا If a letter of madd comes before a changed hamzah, then it is permitted to make qaṣr in it (the madd), (though) madd remains preponderant.[37]

The third word is وَكَأَيّ which comes in seven places: Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 146, Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 105, Sūrat al-Ḥajj, 45, 48, Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, 60, Sūrah Muḥammad ﷺ, 13 and Sūrat al-Ṭalāq, 8. By وَمَدّ, the author indicates that Abū Jaʿfar will add an alif (idkhāl al-alif), exactly like Ibn Kathīr does i.e. وَكَائِٓنْ; the difference being that Abū Jaʿfar makes tashīl in the hamzah. Same as in إِسْرَآئِيلَ, both madd and qaṣr will be allowed.

The fourth word is اللَّآّءِ which comes in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, 4, Sūrat al-Mujādalah, 3 and Sūrat al-Ṭalāq, 4. Abū Jaʿfar will read it without a yāʾ after the hamzah while making tashīl in the hamzah, same as Warsh. He differs with Qālūn who reads the hamzah with taḥqīq. Same as in إِسْرَآئِيلَ, and وَكَآئِنْ, both madd and qaṣr will be allowed.

The fifth word is هٰأَنْتُم which comes in four places: Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 66, 119, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 109 and Sūrah Muḥammad ﷺ, 38. Abū Jaʿfar makes tashīl in the hamzah while reading an alif before it. The author does not clarify whether an alif is read after the hāʾ i.e. between the hāʾ and the hamzah or not, for Abū Jaʿfar; Qālūn reads the alif while Warsh does not. Some have criticized the author for not clarifying this in the reading of Abū Jaʿfar. Perhaps he relies on how the word is pronounced, as in the precept وَبِاللَّفْظِ أَسْتَغْنِيِ عَنِ الْقَيْدِ إِنْ جَلَا (I will suffice myself with the pronunciation of a word without any additional stipulations if it is clear), and therefore felt no need for this clarification.

Yaʿqūb will contradict his basis and read اللَّآّءِ and هٰأَنْتُم with taḥqīq. The pronoun in حَقِّقْهُمَا refers to these two words. Abū ʿAmr has tashīl in both, as well as ibdāl into a yāʾ in the former.

[37] Al-Shāṭibiyyah, line 208.
(Read taḥqīq in) لِئَلَّا for Abū Jaʿfar; make ibdāl (in) the (entire) chapter of النُّبُوءَة and النَّبِيءِ for him (Abū Jaʿfar); and make ibdāl (in) الِّذّئْبَ for Khalaf.

# Commentary

The application regarding لِئَلَّا of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 150, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 165 and Sūrat al-Ḥadīd, 29 is attached to the previous application i.e. read with taḥqīq (حَقِّقْهُمَا). Abū Jaʿfar will therefore contradict Warsh by reading لِئَلَّا with taḥqīq.

The entire chapter of of النُّبُوءَة and النَّبِيءِ, refers to the word النَّبِّي appearing in all its forms: النَّبِيّ, نَبِيّ, نَبِيًّا, النُّبُوَّة, النَّبِيِّين, النَّبِيُّون, الٔانْبِيَاء, أَنْبِيَاء etc. Abū Jaʿfar will contradict his basis and make ibdāl in them. Thus, Abū Jaʿfar, Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will read it the same i.e. like Ḥafṣ would. The pronoun in لَهُ refers to Abū Jaʿfar.

Khalaf will make ibdāl in الِّذّئْب, which comes thrice in Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 13, 14 and 17. In the entire chapter of the hamzah mufradah, Khalaf will agree with his basis except in the word الِّذّئْب.

النَّقْلُ وَالسَّكْتُ وَالْوَقْفُ عَلَى الْهَمْزِ The author combines the chapters of naql, sakt and waqf upon the hamzah in one chapter due to the few differences regarding them between the Three Qurrāʾ.
(There is) no naql, except in الْآنَ, with (that which comes in Sūrah) Yūnus for Ibn Wardān. (Apply) ibdāl in رِدْءًا for Abū Jaʿfar and naql in مِلْءُ for Ibn Wardān.

# Commentary

The author starts by mentioning that generally none of the Three Qurrāʾ have naql. Thereafter, he mentions the exceptions for them, which are five.[38]

The first place is the word الْآنَ which appears in Sūrat al-Baqarah, 71, 187, Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 18, Sūrat al-Anfāl, 66, Sūrah Yūnus عليه السلام, 51, 91, Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 51 and Sūrat al-Jinn, 9. Included with this is آلْآنَ which comes twice in Sūrah Yūnus عليه السلام, 51, 91 (مَعْ يُونُسٍ). The difference between them is that the former is predicated (ikhbār) while the latter is interrogatory (istifhām). In both, Ibn Wardān makes naql. Ibn Wardān therefore contradicts Qālūn in making naql in those places besides Sūrah Yūnus عليه السلام; he also contradicts Warsh by restricting naql to these places. Ibn Jammāz would contradict his basis by reading with taḥqīq in these places.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will agree with their basis and read with taḥqīq.

The second word is رِدْءًا of Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, 34. Abū Jaʿfar will make naql in it, as well as ibdāl of the tanwīn into an alif during waqf and waṣl. This is what author alludes to when he states: وَأَبْدِلْ (and apply ibdāl) i.e. رِدَا يُصَدِّقْنِي. He agrees with Nāfiʿ in making naql, but differs in the ibdāl. Due to ibdāl being mentioned unrestrictedly, it will be applied during waqf and waṣl.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will read like their basis, without naql.

The third word is مِلْءُ الْأْرْضِ of Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 91. Ibn Wardān will make naql during waqf and waṣl i.e. مِلُ الْأْرْضِ. During waqf, he will have the options of iskān, roum or ishmām when stopping on the lām.

Ibn Jammāz, Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will read like their basis, without naql.

The final two words are discussed in the next line.

[38] The word عَادًا الْأْوْلَىَ of Sūrat al-Najm, 50, is excluded from this discussion because Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb both agree with their basis, making naql and idghām i.e. عادً لُّؤْلٰىَ for Qālūn and عادً لُّولٰىَ for Warsh and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī. Abū Jaʿfar would differ from Qālūn in that he makes ibdāl in the hamzah of الاُؤْلَىَ, same as Warsh and Abū ʿAmr. Abū Jaʿfar has three ways of starting from الْأْوْلَىَ of Sūrat al-Najm: 1) Without naql i.e. اَلْأْوْلٰىَ, as Ḥafṣ would start. 2) With naql from the hamzat al-waṣl i.e. اَلُوْلٰىَ. 3) With naql from the circumstancial ḥarakah i.e. لُوْلٰىَ. Khalaf will also agree with his basis and read it like Ḥafṣ, without sakt.
(Make naql in) مِنْ إِسْتَبْرُقٍ for Ruways; (naql in) وَسَلْ and فَسَلْ for Khalaf, taḥqīq of the hamzah during waqf and omit (the application of) sakt (for Khalaf).

# Commentary

The fourth word is مِنْ إِسْتَبْرُقٍ of Sūrat al-Raḥmān, 54. Ruways will read with naql i.e. مِنِ اسْتَبْرُقٍ.

Abū Jaʿfar, Rouḥ and Khalaf will agree with their basis and read without naql. The fifth place in which naql is applied is فَسْئَل and وَسْئَل wherever they appear e.g. وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ, وَسْئَلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا, وَسْئَلُوا اللَه مِنْ فَضْلِهِ, فَسْئَلِ الَّذِّينَ يَقْرَءُونَ الْكِتَابَ, فَسْئَلُوا أَهْلَ الِّذّكْرِ, فَسْئَلُوهُنّ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ etc. Khalaf will make naql in them.

Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb will agree with their basis and read without naql.

In the last half of the line, the author explains that Khalaf will not have takhfīf of the hamzah during waqf – like Ḥamzah has – instead, he will read with taḥqīq. Similarly, he will contradict his basis and not read with sakt before a hamzah e.g. شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ, وَبِالْآخِرَةِ هُم, مَنْ آمَنَ etc. I read without sakt for Khalaf al-ʿĀshir via the Durrāh to my teacher, Qārī Ayyūb.[39] Via the Ṭayyibah, I read with sakt for Idrīs, the transmitter of Khalaf al-ʿĀshir.

الْإِدْغَامُ الصَّغِيُرْ Idghām ṣaghīr refers to the assimilation of two letters, in which the first letter is sākin. It’s discussion may divided into two, the first revolving around the ذ of إِذْ, the د of قَدْ, the feminine ت, the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ. The second is specific words or places in which idghām takes place e.g. وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ, عُذْتُ etc.

[39] Some teachers instructed me to make sakt before the hamzah for Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (Idrīs, the transmitter) when I read to them. Though this might be the practice of some, the textual evidence for not making sakt is too overwhelming to ignore. In the Durrah, Ibn al-Jazarī explicitly states that sakt should be omitted (وَالسَّكْتَ أَهْمُلَا). Ibn al-Jazarī does not mention sakt for Khalaf al-ʿĀshir in Taḥbīr al- Taysīr. The student of Ibn al-Jazarī – as well as the commentator of the Durrah – al-Zabīdī (d. 848 A.H.), explicitly states that no sakt should be made. Bear in mind that al-Zabīdī read the Durrah to Ibn al-Jazarī, as well as the Three Qirāʾāt according to the Durrah to him. If he read with sakt for Khalaf al-ʿĀshir, he would surely have mentioned it. Muḥammad Munayyir al-Samannūdī (d. 1199 A.H.) does not mention sakt for him. In al-Wujūh al-Musfirah, Sheikh al-Mutawallī does not mention sakt either. Though Sheikh al-Ḍabbāʿ and Sheikh ʿAbd al-Rāziq mention sakt, the previously- mentioned textual evidence to apply no sakt cannot be ignored, especially since the practice of most experts have been to read without sakt. And Allah knows best. For further details regarding this discussion, see Taqrīb al-Durrah of Sheikh Īhāb Fikrī.
Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb will make iṭḥ-hār (of the ذ) of إِذْ, with (the د of) قَدْ and the feminine tāʾ; (make iṭḥ-hār) of the tāʾ by the thāʾ for Khalaf.

# Commentary

Idghām of the ذ of إِذْ will take place into 6 letters: ت, ز, ص, د, س and ج e.g. إِذْ تَبَرَّأ, وَاذْ زَيَّنَ, وَإِذْ صَرَفْنَا, إِذْ دَخَلُوا, وَإِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوْهُ and إِذْ جَاءَهُم.

The idghām of the د of قَدْ will take place into 8 letters: س, ذ, ض, ظ, ز, ج, ص and ش e.g. قَدْ سَمِعَ, وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا, قَدْ ضَلُّوا, فَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ, وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَ, لَقَدْ جَاءَكُم, وَلَقَدْ صَرَفْنَا, قَدْ شَغَفَهَا.

Idghām of the feminine tāʾ which is sākinah will take place into 6 letters: س, ث, ص, ز, ظ and ج e.g. أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنَابِلَ, كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُوْدُ, لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ, كُلَّمَا خَبَتْ زِدْنَاهُم, كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً, نَضِجَتْ جُلُوْدُهُم.

Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb will make iṭḥ-hār of the ذ of إِذْ, the د of قَدْ and the feminine tāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar will differ with Warsh in making iṭḥ-hār of the د of قَدْ into the ظ and the ض, as well as the feminine tāʾ into the ظ. However, he will actually agree with his basis in making iṭḥ-hār of the ذ of إِذْ into it’s six letters. Abū ʿAmr makes idghām in all of them.

Khalaf contradicts his bases and makes iṭḥ-hār of the feminine tāʾ by the ث e.g. كَثَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ. He will agree with his basis regarding the remaining five letters into which idghām of the feminine tāʾ is made. Since nothing is mentioned for Khalaf regarding the ذ of إِذْ and the د of قَدْ he will agree with his basis in making idghām of the ذ into the ت and the د; and making idghām of the د into it’s eight letters.

(Make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of) هَلْ and بَلْ for Khalaf. (Make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of) هَلْ (when it appears) with تَرَى, the bāʾ by the fāʾ, (فَنَبَذْتُهَا) نَبَذْتُ, the likes of اِغْفِرْ لِي, يُرِدْ (مَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ) and (كٓهٰيٰعٓصٓ * ذِكْرُ) صَادَ for Yaʿqūb.

# Commentary

In this line the author starts discussing the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ, as well as specific words in which the Three Qurrāʾ will apply iṭḥ-hār and idghām.

The ith-hār of the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ will take place into eight letters: ت, ث, ظ, ز, س, ن, ط and ض. It seems that all eight letters appear after both هَلْ and بَلْ, but this is not the case. Only the ت and ن will come after both هَلْ and بَلْ e.g. هَلْ تَرىٰ, بَلْ تَأْتِيْهْم, هَلْ نُنَبِّؤُكُم, بَلْ نَحْنُ. The ث will only come after the ل of هَلْ e.g. هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ. The remaining five letters – ظ, ز, س, ط and ض – will only appear after بَلْ e.g. بَلْ ظَنَنْتُم, بَلْ زُيِّنَ, بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُم, بَلْ طَبَعَ اللُه, بَلْ ضَلُّوا.

Khalaf will make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ by all it’s letters. Ḥamzah would make idghām into the ث, س and ت.

Yaʿqūb will contradict his basis and make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of هَلْ when it is followed by تَرَى, which is two places: هَلْ تَرَى مِن فُطُور in Sūrat al Mulk, 3, and فَهَلْ لَهُم مِن بِاقِيَة تَرى in Sūrat al Ḥāqqah, 8.

Since nothing is mentioned for Abū Jaʿfar, he will agree with his basis and make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ by all it’s letters. Thus, all Three Qurrāʾ make iṭḥ-hār of the ل of هَلْ and بَلْ.

Subsequently, the author starts discussing individual letters and words in which they have differences.

Yaʿqūb will make iṭḥ-hār of the bāʾ when it meets a fāʾ. In the Qurʾān, the bāʾ majzumah is followed by a fāʾ in five places:

1) Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 74 – أو يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْف.

2) Sūrat al-Raʿd, 5 – وإن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ.

3) Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, 63 – قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَمَنْ تَبِعَكَ.

4) Sūrah Ṭāhā, 97 – قَالَ اذْهَبْ فإنّ لَكَ فِي الْحَياَةِ.

5) Surat al-Ḥujarāt, 11 – وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولَئِكَ.

Since no mention is made of Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf, they will agree with their basis and read with iṭḥ-hār.

Yaʿqūb will also make iṭḥ-hār in فَنَبَذْتُهَا of Sūrah Ṭāhā, 96.

Since nothing is mentioned for Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf, they will agree with their basis; Abū Jaʿfar making iṭḥ-hār and Khalaf making idghām.

The كَ of كَاغْفِرْ in the verse indicates a comparison (لِلتَّشْبِيه) i.e. the ‚likes of اِغْفِرْ لِي‛. Yaʿqūb will make iṭḥ-hār of the likes of اِغْفِرْ لِي i.e. the rāʾ majzūmah into the lām e.g. وَاصِبْرُ لِحُكْمِ, يَغْفِرْ لَكُم. Al-Dūrī has idghām with an option of iṭḥ-hār while al-Sūsī only has idghām.

Since nothing is mentioned for Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf, they will both agree with their basis and make iṭḥ-hār. Thus, all Three Qurrāʾ have iṭḥ-hār here.

Yaʿqūb will contradict his basis and make iṭḥ-hār of the د in مَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ of Sūrah Āli ‘Imrān, 145.

Since nothing is mentioned for Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf, they will agree with their basis; Abū Jaʿfar making iṭḥ-hār and Khalaf making idghām.

Yaʿqūb will also make iṭḥ-hār of the ṣād in كٓهٰيٰعٓصٓ * ذِكْرُ at the start of Sūrah Maryam.

Since nothing is mentioned for Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf, they will agree with their basis; Abū Jaʿfar making iṭḥ-hār and Khalaf making idghām.

(Make iṭḥ-hār in) أَخَذْتُ for Ruways, (iṭḥ-hār in) (أَورِثْتُمُوهَا) أُورِثْتُمْ for Yaʿqūb and Khalaf, as well as (iṭḥ-hār in) لَبِثْتُ for both of them (Yaʿqūb and Khalaf); make idghām (in the latter i.e. لَبِثْتُ) with عُذْتُ for Abū Jaʿfar, and this (عُذْتُ) is the opposite for Yaʿqūb (i.e. iṭḥ-hār).

# Commentary

Ruways will contradict his basis and make iṭḥ-hār in أَخَذْتُ in all its forms whether singular or plural e.g. اتَّخَذْتُم, اَخَذْتُم, اتَّخَذْت, وَأَخَذْتُهَا etc. Though the author only mentions أَخَذْتُ, it is well-known that the iṭḥ-hār is made by Ruways in all its forms.

Abū Jaʿfar, Rouḥ and Khalaf will agree with their basis and make idghām.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will make iṭḥ-hār of the ث by the ت in أَورِثْتُمُوهَا of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 43 and Sūrat al-Zukhruf, 72.

Abū Jaʿfar will agree with his basis and make iṭḥ-hār. Thus, all Three Qurrāʾ will have iṭḥ-hār here.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will also have iṭḥ-hār of the ث of لَبِثْتُ and لَبِثْتَ; whether singular or plural e.g. لَبِثْتُم.

Abū Jaʿfar will make idghām in لَبِثْتُ, لَبِثْتَ, لَبِثْتُم – however they may appear – as well as idghām of the ذ into the ت in عُذْتُ of Sūrah Ghāfir, 27 and Sūrat al-Dukhān, 20.

Yaʿqūb will read the opposite of idghām in عُذْتُ i.e. he will read it with iṭḥ-hār.

Khalaf will agree with his basis and make idghām in عُذْتُ.

Make idghām in (يٰسٓ وَالْقُرْان) يَاسِيَن and (نٓ وَالْقَلَمِ) نُونَ for Khalaf and Yaʿqūb, as well as (idghām) in (طٰسٓمٓ) سِيَن مِيَم for Khalaf; (make) iṭḥ-hār in (يَلْهَثْ ذٰلِكَ) يَلْهَثَ for Abū Jaʿfar and (iṭḥ-hār) in (اِرْكَبْ مَعَنَا) ارْكَبْ for Khalaf and Abū Jaʿfar.

# Commentary

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will make idghām in يٰسٓ وَالْقُرْان and نٓ وَالْقَلَمِ.

In (سِيْنْ مِّيْم) طٰسٓمٓ, Khalaf will contradict his basis and make idghām.

Yaʿqūb will agree with his basis and make idghām.

Abū Jaʿfar will only have iṭḥ-hār in all the above places because he makes sakt on the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt. Madd lāzim ḥarfī muthaqqal will therefore not be found in the Qirāʾah of Abū Jaʿfar.

In يَلْهَثْ ذٰلِكَ of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 176, Abū Jaʿfar will have iṭḥ-hār. Warsh will also have iṭḥ-hār while Qālūn has a choice of iṭḥ-hār as well as idghām.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will agree with their basis and make idghām.

In اِرْكَبْ مَعَنَا of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام, 42, Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf will have iṭḥ-hār. Warsh will also have iṭḥ-hār while Qālūn has a choice of iṭḥ-hār as well as idghām.

Yaʿqūb will agree with his basis and make idghām.

النُّونُ السَّاكِنَةُ وَالتَّنْوِينُ

(Apply) ghunnah by the yāʾ and the wāw for Khalaf; and (apply) ikhfāʾ by the khāʾ and the ghayn for Abū Jaʿfar, except in (إِنْ يَّكُنْ غَنِيًّا) يَكُنْ,(فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ) يُنْغِضْ and (وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ) مُنْخَنِقْ.

# Commentary

Khalaf will make idghām with ghunnah when the nūn sākinah or the tanwīn is followed by a yāʾ or a wāw, contradicting his basis.

Likewise, Yaʿqūb and Abū Jaʿfar will agree with their basis and make idghām with ghunnah.

Abū Jaʿfar will make ikhfāʾ when the nūn sākinah or the tanwīn is followed by a ghayn or a khāʾ e.g. مِنْ خَيْرْ, هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرْ اللِه, مِنْ غَيْرِكْمْ, يَوْمَئِذٍ خَاشِعَةٌ, نُزُلًا مِنْ غَفُورٍ رَّحِيم. There are three places which are excluded: فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, 51, إِنْ يَّكُنْ غَنِيًّا of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 135 and وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 3. In these three places, as well as the remaining four letters of the throat, Abū Jaʿfar will read with iṭḥ-hār.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will agree with their basis and make iṭḥ-hār by all six letters of the throat.

تْالْفَحُ وَالْإِمَةُالَ Though the Three Qurrāʾ apply fatḥ and imālah, none of them has taqlīl.

(Read) with fatḥ in قَهَّارِ, الْبَوَارِ and ضِعَافَ, (as well as) the middle of the trilateral (verbs) with it; (except) رَانَ, شَآءَ and جَآءَ, make imālah (in them). (Make imālah in) the likes of الٔابْرَارِ, رُؤْيَا (with) اللَّام and التَّورَاة for Khalaf. Do not make imālah for Yaʿqūb, except (for) أَعْمْٰى in the first place in (Sūrah) Subḥān.

# Commentary

Khalaf will differ with his basis and read with fatḥ in القَهَّارِ which comes in two places: وَبَرَزُوا لِله الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 48 and لِله الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ of Sūrah Ghāfir, 16. He will also have fatḥ in البَوَارِ of دَارَ الْبَوَارِ, in Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 28 and ضِعَافًا of ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا, in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 9. Ḥamzah makes taqlīl in الْقَهَّارِ, البَوَارِ and makes imālah in ضِعَافًا, with Khallād having a choice of fatḥ.

Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will make imālah in three of the 10 trilateral past tense verbs that Ḥamzah makes imālah in; رَانَ, جَآءَ and شَآءَ.[40] In the remaining seven words he will have fatḥ.

He will also make imālah in the likes of الٔابْرَارِ of Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 193, 198 and Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn, 18. ‚The likes of الٔابْرَارِ‛ includes all those alifs which appear between two rāʾ’s, the second one being majrūr, whether maʿrifah or nakirah e.g. الٔاشْرَارِ of Sūrah Ṣād, 62, مِنْ قَرَارِ of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 26, etc. Ḥamzah makes taqlīl in these words.

Khalaf will furthermore make imālah in الرَّؤْيَا, only when it appears with اللَّام i.e. when it is maʿrifah due to lām al-taʿrīf being attached. Thus, in رُءْيٰيَ and رُءْيَاكَ he will not make imālah. Ḥamzah reads with fatḥ in all these words.

In التَّورَاة, Khalaf will contradict his basis and make imālah while Ḥamzah reads it with taqlīl.

Besides the above-mentioned places, Khalaf will make imālah in all those words in which his basis makes imālah in e.g. الفَتٰى, الٔانْثٰى, بَلٰى, الٔاعْلٰى, اشْتَرٰى etc.

After completing the discussions pertaining to Khalaf, the author starts explaining the words in which Yaʿqūb has imālah. Yaʿqūb will not make imālah in any of the alifs in which Abū ʿAmr makes imālah or taqlīl in, except the first أَعْمْٰى of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, 72 (بِسُبْحَانَ أَوَّلَا).

The matters pertaining to the reading of Yaʿqūb are continued in the next line.

[40] The 10 trilateral past tense verbs in which Ḥamzah makes imālah in are خَابَ, خَافَ, طَابَ, ضَاقَتْ, حَاقَ, زَاغَ, جَآءَ, شَآءَ, زَادَ, رَانَ.
And for Ruways (make imālah in) كَافِرِينَ, all of them; and in (Sūrah) al-Naml for Yaʿqūb; as well as the yāʾ of يَاسِيَن for Rouḥ. (Make) fatḥ in the entire chapter for the noble Abū Jaʿfar.

# Commentary

Ruways will make imālah in كَافِرِينَ and الكَافِرِينَ. الْكُلّ in the line includes both nakirah and maʿrifah, wherever they may appear in the Qurʾān.

In إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِنْ قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ of Sūrat al-Naml, 43, Yaʿqūb – both Ruways and Rouḥ – will make imālah in كَافِرِينَ. This is what the author intends when he states: ‚ وَالنَّمْلَ حُطْ‛ i.e. the كَافِرِينَ of Sūrat al-Naml.

Rouḥ will contradict his basis and make imālah in the yāʾ of يٰسٓ. Abū ʿAmr reads it with fatḥ.

To summarise Yaʿqūb’s reading: of all the places that Abū ʿAmr has imālah, Yaʿqūb will only agree with him in the first أَعْمْٰى of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, generally in كَافِرِينَ for Ruways, and specifically the كَافِرِينَ of Sūrat al-Naml for Yaʿqūb (both Ruways and Rouḥ) and the yāʾ of يٰسٓ.

Abū Jaʿfar does not read with imālah at all (وَافْتَحِ الْبَابَ اذْ).

الرَّاءَاتُ وَالَّلامَاتُ وَالْوَقْفُ عَلَى الْمَرْسُومِ The author combines a few chapters together because of the few differences regarding them amongst the Three Qurrāʾ.

Recite the rāʾ’s and the lāms like Qālūn for Abū Jaʿfar. Stop on يَا أَبَهْ with a hāʾ for Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb; (stop) on لِمَ… And its remaining words like al-Bazzī (does) for Yaʿqūb, along with هُوَ, هِيَ; and erudites relate (the same on) the likes of عَلَيْهْنَّهْ and إِلَيَّهْ for him (Yaʿqūb).

# Commentary

Abū Jaʿfar will differ with Warsh and read the rāʾ’s and the lāms like Qālūn i.e. he will not have the conventional taghlīṭḥ of the lam or tarqīq of the rāʾ that Warsh has e.g. بَصِيرًا, بَصِيٌرْ بِمَا, الصَّلَاة, الطَّلَاق, ظَلَمْتُم.

Yaʿqūb and Khalaf will agree with their basis and read the same.

From the second half of the line, the author starts discussing waqf of the Three Qurrāʾ according to the rasm (ʿUthmānic script).

Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb will stop with a hāʾ on يَا أَبَتِ which comes appears eight times in four sūrahs: Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 4, 100, Sūrah Maryam, 42, 43, 44, 45, Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, 26 and Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt, 102.

Khalaf will agree with his basis and stop with a tāʾ.

At the end of the line, and the line that follows, the author starts explaining four instances in which Yaʿqūb will stop with hāʾ al-sakt.

The first is when stopping on the interrogatory mā (mā istifhāmiyyah – مَا), which alif is dropped due a preposition (حُرُوف الْجَرّ) being attached to it. This takes place in five words. The author mentions one i.e. لِمَ, but alludes to the others by stating وَسَائِرُهَا – its remaining words. Imam al-Shāṭibī mentions these five words for al-Bazzī in the following line:

يوَفِمَهْ وَمِمَّهْ قِفْ وَعَمَّهْ لِمَهْ بِمَهْ بِ * خُلْفٍ عَنِ الْبَزِّيّ وَادْفَعْ مُجَهِّلَا (Waqf as) فِيمَهْ, مِمَّهْ, عَمَّهْ, لِمَهْ and بِمَهْ is related from al-Bazzī with a choice, and repel the ignorant one (concerning this).[41] Yaʿqūb will stop like al-Bazzī on these five words i.e. with hāʾ al-sakt on examples like لِمَ تَقُولُونَ, فِيَم أَنْتَ مِنْ ذِكْرَاهَا, فَلْيَنْظُرِ الْإِنْسَانُ مِمّ خُلِقَ, عَمّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ, بِمَ يَرْجِعُ الْمُرْسَلُونَ. When the author mentions that Yaʿqūb will read like al-Bazzī on these words, it seems that he will also have a choice of reading without the hāʾ al-sakt as well, like al-Bazzī has via the Shāṭibiyyah. Some commentaries, like al-Ghurrat al-Bahiyyah, relate this choice for Yaʿqūb as well. However, Yaʿqūb will not have a choice i.e. he will only stop with hāʾ al-sakt on these words since the Taḥbīr does not mention an option for al-Bazzī on these words, neither does the Taysīr.[42]

The second instance where Yaʿqūb will stop with hāʾ al-sakt is on the third person singular pronoun – masculine or feminine – i.e. هُوَ and هِيَ, whether attached to a wāw, fāʾ or lām e.g. فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُ هُوَ, يُبَيِّنُ لَنَا مَا هِيَ, وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ, وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِم, فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُم, فَهِيَي كَالْحِجَارَةِ, لَهُوَ الْغَنِيّ, لَهِييَ الْحَيَوَانُ. The author alludes to this by stating مَعْ هُو وَهِي.

The third instance where he stops with a hāʾ al-sakt is the nūn mushaddadah that comes after the hāʾ of the third person feminine plural pronoun, whether it is attached to a verb e.g. عَلِمْتُمُوهُنّ, أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنّ, لَا تُخْرِجُوهُنّ, a noun e.g. بُيُوتِهِنّ, نِسَآءِهِنّ, أَبْصَارِهِنّ or a particle e.g. لَهُنّ, مِنْهُنّ, عَلَيْهُنّ, إِلَيْهُنّ, فِيهُنّ. The nūn mushaddadad which is not in a pronoun is excluded e.g. وَلَا يَحْزَنّ. With the clause ‚that comes after the hāʾ‛, the nūn mushaddadah that comes after a kāf or tāʾ are excluded i.e. Yaʿqūb will not stop with a hāʾ al-sakt on it e.g. إِنّ كَيْدَكُنّ, مِنْكُنّ, إِنْ كُنْتُنّ, لَسْتُنّ. However, in مِنْ كَيْدِكُنّ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام,[43] there is difference of opinion. Sheikh Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Khalījī and Sheikh ʿAbd al-Fattāḥ al-Qāḍī, amongst others, view that the hāʾ al-sakt should not be read because Ibn al-Jazarī states in the Nashr:[44] لَثَّداً مَحَأ دْجِأ مْلَوَ هِوا بِلُثَّا مَمَكَ اءٍهَ دَعْبَ نَا كَامَبِ هُيدُيِقْتَ ابَوَالصّ نَّأ بُسِحْأَم وَهُضُعْبَ هُقَلَطْأ دْقَوَ بِغَيْرْ ذٰلِكَ ‚Some have mentioned it unrestrictedly; I deem that what is correct is to restrict it to that which comes after a hāʾ, as in the examples they have presented. I have not found anyone giving examples contradicting this‛.[45] Sheikh Muḥammad Ibrāhīm[46] observes stopping with hāʾ al-sakt on مِنْ كَيْدِكُنّ since Sheikh al-Mutawallī presents it as an example in al-Wujūh al-Musfirah.[47] Sheikh Īhāb Fikrī and Sheikh ʿAbd al-Rāziq allow both ways: stopping with the hāʾ al-sakt as well as stopping without the hāʾ al-sakt. They reason that Ibn al-Jazarī himself gives the example of مِنْ كَيْدِكُنّ in Taḥbīr al-Taysīr stating: وَ"مِنْ كَيْدِكُنّ"عَلَى قَوْلِ عَامَّةِ أَهْلِ الْأْدَاءِ ‚مِنْ كَيْدِكُنّ (stop with a hāʾ) according to most experts.‛[48] Sheikh Īhāb Fikrī further elucidates that one should bear in mind that the Durrah was written 24 years after the Ṭayyibah,[49] and the Taḥbir is considered the source text for the Durrah.[50] If this is the practice of most experts (عَامَّةِ أَهْلِ الْأْدَاءِ), then the practice of others (غَيْرْ عَامَّةِ أَهْلِ الْأْدَاءِ) would be without the hāʾ al-sakt. And Allah knows best.[51]

The fourth instance is the yāʾ mutakallim that is mushaddadah e.g. يُوحَىَ إِلَيّ, أَلَّا تَعْلُوا عَلَيّ, خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيّ, مَا يُبَدَّلُ الْقَوْلُ لَدَيّ, بِمُصْرِخِيّ.

(Stop with hāʾ al-sakt on) the words of lamentation, along with ثَمّ for Ruways. Be sure to omit the hāʾ in سُلْطَانِيَهْ, (مَالِيَهْ) مَا لِي and (مَا هِيَهْ) مَا هِيَ when joining… For Yaʿqūb; and affirm (them i.e. the three words mentioned) for Khalaf. Likewise, omit (the hāʾ in) كِتَابِيَهْ, (فِبِهُدٰيُهمُ اقْتَدِهْ) اقْتَدْ,(لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ) تَسَنّ,(حِسَابِيَهْ) حِسَابِي when joining for Yaʿqūb.

# Commentary

On the words of lamentation, which the author alludes to by stating ‚ذُو نُدْبَةٍ‛, Ruways will stop with a hāʾ al-sakt. These words are three: يَا أَسَفٰى, يَا حَسْرْتٰى and يَا وَيْلَتٰى e.g. يٰأَسَفٰى عَلٰى يُوسُفَ, يٰحَسْرْتٰى عَلٰى مَا فَرَّطْتّ, يٰوَيْلَتٰى لَيْتَنِيِ. Note, that when stopping on these words, one would read with ṭūl since the alif is followed by a hāʾ al-sakt which always has a sukūn.

Similarly, Ruways will stop on ثَمّ, the adverb (ṭḥarf), with hāʾ al-sakt i.e. ثَمَّهْ e.g. فَثَمّ وَجْهُ اللِه, وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمّ الْآخَرِينَ, وَإِذَا رَأْيْتَ ثَمّ رَأَيْتَ, مُطَاعٍ ثَمّ أَمِيَن.

During waṣl, Ruways will read without the hāʾ al-sakt on these words. Abū Jaʿfar, Rouḥ and Khalaf will agree with their basis in these words.

Thereafter, the author discusses seven words that come in nine places, in which the hāʾ al-sakt is written in the Qurʾān. Their sequence of mentioning in the poem is as follows:

1) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 29 – 30 – عَنِّيِ سُلْطٰنِيَهْ خُذُوهُ.

2) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 28 – 29 – عَنِّيِ مَالِيَهْ هَلَكَ.

3) Sūrat al-Qāriʿah, 10 – 11 – مَا هِيَهْ نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ.

4) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 19 – 20 – اِقْرَءُوا كِتَابِيَهْ إِنِّي ظَنَنْتُ.

5) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 25 – 26 – لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ وَلَمْ أَدْرِ.

6) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 20 – 21 – أَنِّي مُلٰقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ فَهُوَ فِي.

7) Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, 26 – 27 – وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ يٰلَيْتَهَا.

8) Sūrat al-Baqarah, 259 – لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ وَانْظُرْ.

9) Sūrat al-Anʿām, 90 – فِبِهُدٰيُهمُ اقْتَدِهْ قُلَّا أَسْئَلُكُم.

Bear in mind that the differences between all Ten Qurrāʾ in these seven words are always during waṣl. During waqf, all will read the hāʾ al-sakt.

Yaʿqūb will drop the hāʾ al-sakt during waṣl in all nine places. The first three places are mentioned in وَلِهَا احْذِفَنْ بِسُلْطَانِيَهْ مَا لِي وَمَا هِيَ مُوصِلَا حِمَاهُ. The remaining places are mentioned in كَذَا احْذِفْ كِتَابِيَهْ حِسَابَي تَسَنّ اقْتَدْ لَدَى الْوَصْلِ حُفِّلَا. مُوصِلَا and لَدَى الْوَصْلِ indicates that ḥadhf will only take place during waṣl. The kāf of كَذَا is to draw a comparison i.e. in the same manner that Yaʿqūb made ḥadhf in the first three words, he will make in the latter words as well.

Khalaf will make ithbāt of the hāʾ al-sakt during waṣl and waqf in the first three places. This is understood from: وَأَثْبِتْ فُزْ i.e. make ithbāt for Khalaf. The places in which he makes ithbāt in are those places mentioned earlier i.e. وَلِهَا احْذِفَنْ بِسُلْطَانِيَهْ مَا لِي وَمَا هِيَ. Ḥamzah makes ḥadhf of the hāʾ during waṣl in these three places. In the remaining six places he will agree with his basis i.e. in كِتَابِيَهْ and حِسَابِيَهْ, Khalaf will have ithbāt during waṣl, while in the last two he will have ḥadhf during waṣl.

Abū Jaʿfar will agree with his basis and have ithbāt during waṣl and waqf in all nine places.
(Stop on) أَيًّاَ in أَيًّاَ مَّا for Ruways, and on مَا for Khalaf; and (stop) on the yāʾ if it has been omitted due to it being sākin for Yaʿqūb.

# Commentary

In أَيًّاَ مَّا تَدْعُوا of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, 110, Ruways stops on أَيًّاَ while Khalaf stops on the مَا. They both differ with their basis while Abū Jaʿfar and Rouḥ will agree with their basis.

Even though this precept is mentioned for them in texts, Ibn al-Jazarī allows waqf on either one of the two for all Ten Qurrāʾ since they are written separately.[52]

If a yāʾ has been omitted from writing due to two sākin letters meeting (ijtimāʾ al-sākinayn), except in the case of a tanwīn e.g. فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ, وَالٍ, then Yaʿqūb will read that yāʾ during waqf. Examples of this come in the next line.

[52] Al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pp. 144-145.
Like تُغْنِ النُّذُرْ and مَنْ يُؤْتَ with a kasrah (مَنْ يُؤْتِ الْحِكْمْةَ), (stop on) the lām of مَالِ, along with وَيْكَأَنَّهْ and وَيْكَأَنّ; in this manner it is read.

# Commentary

The author mentions two examples of the yāʾ being dropped in the rasm, yet read by Yaʿqūb during waqf upon these words. The first example is تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ of Sūrat al-Qamar, 5. During waqf, Yaʿqūb will read the yāʾ i.e. تُغْنِيْ. This yāʾ is omitted in the rasm, as well as in recitation during waṣl for all the qurrāʾ. The second example is وَمَنْ يُؤْتِ الْحِكْمْةَ of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 269. Yaʿqūb reads the tāʾ with a kasrah; the author alludes to this by stating ‚وَاكْسِرْ‛. Thus, during waqf, Yaʿqūb will stop with the yāʾ i.e. يُؤْتِيْ. This application for Yaʿqūb occurs in 11 words that come in 17 places:

1) Sūrat al-Baqarah, 269 – وَمَنْ يُؤْتِ الْحِكْمْةَ.

2) Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 146 – وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللُه.

3) Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 3 – وَاخْشَونِ الْيَوْمَ.

4) Sūrat al-Anʿām, 57 – يَقُصّ الْحَقّ (Yaʿqūb reads يَقْضِ الْحَقّ).

5) Sūrah Yūnus عليه السلام, 103 – نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِيَن.

6) Sūrat al-Naml, 18 – وَادِ النَّمْلِ.

7) Sūrah Ṭāhā, 12 – بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ.

8) Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt, 16 – بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ.

9) Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, 30 – الْوَادِ الْأْيْمَنِ.

10) Sūrat al-Ḥajj, 54 – لَهَادِ الَّذِّينَ.

11) Sūrat al-Rūm, 53 – بِهٰدِ الْعُمْيِ.

12) Sūrah Yāsīn, 23 – يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمَٰنُ.

13) Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt, 163 – صَالِ الْجَحِيِم.

14) Sūrah Qāf, 41 – يُنَادِ الْمُنَادِ.

15) Sūrat al-Qamar, 5 – تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ.

16) Sūrat al-Raḥmān, 24 – الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَئَاتُ.

17) Sūrat al-Takwīr, 16 – الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ.[53] In all the above-mentioned places Yaʿqūb will read the yāʾ during waqf.

Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf will agree with their basis and stop without the yāʾ.

Thereafter, the author discusses the word مَالِ which comes in four places in the Qurʾān:

1) Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, 78 – فَمَالِ هٰؤُلَآءِ.

2) Sūrat al-Kahf, 49 – مَالِ هٰذَا الْكِتَابِ.

3) Sūrat al-Furqān, 7 – مَالِ هٰذَا الرَّسُولِ.

4) Sūrat al-Maʿārij, 36 – فَمَالِ الَّذِّينَ كَفَرُوا.

In these four places Yaʿqūb will stop on the lām.

Even though this documented for Yaʿqūb, Ibn al-Jazarī relates waqf on either one of the two for all Ten Qurrāʾ since they are written separately.[54] In وَيْكَأَنّ اللَه يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ and وَيْكَأَنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ of Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ, 82, Yaʿqūb will stop on the nūn of وَيْكَأَنّ and on the hāʾ of وَيْكَأَنَّهْ. He differs with his basis who stops on the kāf.

Abū Jaʿfar and Khalaf agree with their basis, stopping in the same manner Yaʿqūb does.

يَاءَاتُ الْإِضَافَةِ The yāʾāt al-iḍāfah is yāʾ mutakallim, which can appear on a noun, verb or particle. A kāf, hāʾ or any other pronoun may assume the place of the yāʾ mutakallim, and it does not form part of the original word i.e. it does not fall on any of the root-letters (the fāʾ, ʿayn or lām kalimah) e.g. إِنِّي, إِنَّهُ, إِنَّكَ, ذِكْرِي, ذِكْرُهُ, ذِكْرُكَ, سَتَجِدُنَي, سَتَجِدُهُ, سَتَجِدُكَ. The differences that the qurrāʾ have concerning the yāʾ al-iḍāfah, are whether it should be read as maftūḥah or sākinah.

Their differences are found in 212 yāʾ’s and may be divided as follows:[55]

1) The yāʾ al-iḍāfah is followed by a hamzat al-qaṭ‘, which is maftūḥah. This is found in 99 places.[56]

2) The yāʾ al-iḍāfah followed by hamzat al-qaṭʿ, which is maksūrah. They total 52.[57]

3) The yāʾ followed by hamzat al-qaṭʿ, which is maḍmūmah. They amount to 10.

4) The yāʾ followed by hamzat al-waṣl, which is lām al-taʿrīf. They are 14.

5) The yāʾ followed by hamzat al-waṣl, which is not lām al-taʿrīf. They count 7.

6) The yāʾ which is not followed by a hamzah. This type amounts to 30.

[54] Al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pp. 146-147.

[55] This is according to the categories and count in the Shāṭibiyyah.

[56] Nāfīʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr generally read this category of yāʾ as maftūḥah, with exceptions.

[57] Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr generally read this category of yāʾ as maftūḥah, with a few exceptions.
Abū Jaʿfar will read like Qālūn (except in) لِيْ دِينِ; read it with iskān. Read إِخْوَتِي and رَبِّي with a fatḥah for Abū Jaʿfar. Read the entire chapter with iskān for Yaʿqūb.

# Commentary

Abū Jaʿfar will read like Qālūn in all six categories of the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah as it comes in the Shāṭibiyyah. He differs with Qālūn in three instances:

1) وَلِيْ دِينِ – Sūrat al-Kāfirūn, 6.

Abū Jaʿfar will differ with Nāfiʿ and read it as sākin (لِي دِينِ سَكِّنْ). Nāfiʿ reads it with a fatḥah.

2) وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي إِنّ – Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 100.

3) وَلَئِنْ رُّجِعْتُ الٰىَ رَبِّي إِنّ – Sūrah Fuṣṣilat, 50.

Abū Jaʿfar will read the above two places with a fatḥah (وَإِخْوَتِي وَرَبِّي افْتَحَ اصْلًا). In number two he differs with Qālūn and agrees with Warsh, while in number three he differs with Qālūn in one of his options.

Thereafter, the author mentions a general precept for Yaʿqūb; he will read the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah in all six categories as sākin (وَاسْكِنِ الْبَابَ حُمِّلَا). In the next line, he mentions the exceptions to this precept.

(Read the entire chapter with iskān for Yaʿqūb) except by the lām al-ʿurf (lām al-taʿrīf), excluding (the cases of vocation), as well as (excluding) مَحْيَايَ and مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمَهُ. Be sure to omit that which follows…

# Commentary

Yaʿqūb will generally read the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah in all the categories as sākin. In this line a few exceptions to this general precept are mentioned.

The first exception is the yāʾ al-iḍāfah which is followed by a lām al-tāʾrif (سِوَى عِنْدَ لَامِ الْعُرْفِ). They total 14, in which he will read with a fatḥah during waṣl. From this exception, two places in which vocation occurs (إِلَّا النِّدَا) are excluded: يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ ءَامَنُوا of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, 56 and يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ أَسْرَفُوا of Sūrat al-Zumar, 53. In these two places, Yaʿqūb will read the yāʾ with a sukūn as per his conventional practice i.e. iskān, as mentioned in line 52.

Two further exceptions to his general precept mentioned are وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي of Sūrat al-Anʿām, 162 (وَغَيْرْ مَحْيَايَ) and مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمَهُ of Sūrat al-Ṣaff, 6 (وَغَيْرْ... مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمَهُ). In these two places, Yaʿqūb will agree with his basis and read with a fatḥah on the yāʾ. The reason it is mentioned here is to exclude it from his general precept of reading with iskān.

At the end of the line, he mentions that ḥadhf will be made in a word which is mentioned in the next line, as well as for whom.

(Be sure to omit that which follows in:) (يٰعِبٰدِ لَا خَوْفٌ) عِبَادِيَ لَا for Rouḥ; read with a fatḥah قَوْمِي for him (Rouḥ); (read with a fatḥah) قُلْ لِّعِبَادِي for Ruways and Khalaf; and he (Khalaf) has compliance (in reading with a fatḥah)…

# Commentary

Excluded from the general precept mentioned for Yaʿqūb i.e. to read the yāʾ al-iḍāfah with iskān is عِبَادِي which comes with لَا i.e. يٰعِبٰدِ لَا خَوْفٌ of Sūrat al-Zukhruf,

68. With the clause عِبَادِي) عِبَادِيَ لَا which comes with لَا), other places where عِبَادِي comes are excluded e.g. يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ ءَامَنُوا, يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ أَسْرَفُوا. In Sūrat al-Zukruf, Rouḥ will not read the yāʾ - making ḥadhf of the yāʾ - during waqf and waṣl.

Ruways will read the yāʾ as sākinah, according to his precept.

In إِنّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا of Sūrat al-Furqān, 30, Rouḥ will read the yāʾ with a fatḥah (وَقَوْمِي افْتَحًا لَهُ). The pronoun in لَهُ refers to Rouḥ. He actually agrees with his basis, but it needed to be mentioned to exclude it from the general precept of iskān given for Yaʿqūb. Ruways maintains his precept of reading it with a sukūn.

In قُلْ لِّعِبَادِيَ الَّذِّينَ ءَامَنُوا of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 31, Ruways and Khalaf will read the yāʾ with a fatḥah during waṣl. During waqf, they will both read it with a sukūn. Ruways actually agrees with the rule mentioned for him earlier i.e سِوَى عِنْدَ لَامِ الْعُرْفِ. Thus, there is really no need to mention this for Ruways because according to the rules mentioned previously, he will read this yāʾ with a fatḥah. Why mention it again? # Commentary

Khalaf will read the yāʾ al-iḍāfah which is followed by a lām al-taʿrīf with a fatḥah. They are in 14 places:

1) Sūrat al-Baqarah, 124 – عَهْدِيَ الظَّالِمِيْن.

2) Sūrat al-Baqarah, 258 – رَبِّيَ الَّذِّي يُحْيِيِ وَيُمِيتُ.

3) Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 33 – حَرَّمَ رَبِّيَ الْفَوَاحِشَ.

4) Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 146 – سَأَصْرِفُ عَنْ أٰيَاتِيَ الَّذِّينَ يَتَكَبَّرَُوُنَ.

5) Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 31 – قُلْ لِّعِبَادِيَ الَّذِّينَ أٰمَنُوا.

6) Sūrah Maryam, 30 – ءَاتَانِيَ الْكِتَاب.

7) Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, 83 – مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرّ.

8) Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, 105 – عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُوْن.

9) Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, 56 – يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ أٰمَنُوا إِنّ أَرْضِي.

10) Sūrah Sabaʾ, 13 – عِبَادِيَ الشَّكُوْر.

11) Sūrah Ṣād, 41 – مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَان.

12) Sūrat al-Zumar, 38 – إِنْ أَرَادَنِيَ اللُه بِضُّرّ.

13) Sūrat al-Zumar, 53 – يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّيْنَ أَسْرَفُوا.

14) Sūrat al-Mulk, 28 – إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِيَ الله.

Khalaf will read all the above places with a fatḥah on the yāʾ al-iḍāfah, except in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt and the second place in Sūrat al-Zumar, where it comes as vocation (nidāʾ) i.e. يٰعِبٰدِيَ. This is what is meant by لَا النِّدَا (except the vocation). Thus, Khalaf differs with his basis in 12 places and agrees with him in these two places.

Synopsis of the applications for the Three Qurrāʾ Abū Jaʿfar reads like Qālūn in all six categories except in three places: وَلِيْ دِينِ, وَبَيْنَ إِخْوَتِي إِنّ and وَلَئِنْ رُّجِعْتُ لٰيَإ رَبِّي إِنّ.

Yaʿqūb will generally read all five categories with iskān, except the yāʾ followed by lām al-taʿrīf which he will read with a fatḥah; excluding two places from it followed by vocation i.e. يٰعِبٰدِي الَّذِّينَ ءَامَنُوا and يٰعِبٰدِي الَّذِّينَ أَسْرَفُوا, which he will also read with a sukūn. He will further read وَمَحْيَايَ and مِنْ بَعْدِي اسْمَهُ with a fatḥah. Rouḥ will drop the yāʾ in يٰعِبٰدِ لَا خَوْفٌ during waqf and waṣl, while Ruways will read it with a sukūn during waqf and waṣl. Rouḥ will read إِنّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا with a fatḥah while Ruways would read the yāʾ with a sukūn. In قُلْ لِّعِبَادِيَ الَّذِّينَ ءَامَنُوا Ruways will read the yāʾ with a fatḥah during waṣl and Rouḥ will read it with iskān.

Khalaf will read the three categories in which it is followed a hamzat al-qaṭʿ with iskān. The category in which the yāʾ is followed by a hamzat al-waṣl which is not a lām al-taʿrīf, he will also read it with iskān. In the category followed by lām al-taʿrīf, he will read the yāʾ with a fatḥah except in يٰعِبٰدِيَ الَّذِّينَ of Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt and the second place of Sūrat al-Zumar. In the category in which it is not followed by a hāmzah – which are 30 places – he reads مَحْيَايَ with a fatḥah and omits the yāʾ of يٰعِبٰدِ لَا خَوْفٌ. In the remaining 28 places he will read with iskān. الْيَاءَاتُ الزَّوَائِدُ Yāʾāt al-zawāʾid refer to those yāʾ’s which are not written in the muṣḥaf but are read by the qurrāʾ. Hence they are called the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid (the additional yāʾ’s) because they are added in recitation, though they are not written.[59]

The difference that the qurrāʾ have regarding them is whether to read them or not i.e. make ithbāt or ḥadhf of them; either during waṣl and waqf, during waṣl only or during waqf only.[60]

The difference between the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid and yāʾāt al-iḍāfah are five:

1) The yāʾāt al-zawāʾid comes in nouns e.g. الَّدَاعِ, الْجَوَارِ and in verbs e.g. يَوْمَ يَأْتِ, وَالَّيْلِ اذَا يَسْرْ, but do not come in particles. The yāʾāt al-iḍāfah will come in particles as well.

2) The yāʾāt al-zawāʾid are not written in the muṣḥaf while the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah are.

3) The differences that the qurrāʾ have regarding the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid are whether they should be read or not, while the differences that they have regarding the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah are whether they should be read as sākinah or as maftūḥah.[61]

4) The yāʾāt al-zawāʾid are aṣliyyah or zāʾidah – as will be made clear later – while the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah are always zāʾidah (not part of the root-letters).

5) The differences applied to the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid are during waṣl and waqf whereas in the yāʾāt al-iḍāfah it is applied during waṣl only.[62] The total number of yāʾāt al-zawāʾid is 123.[63] They are divided into two categories, those appearing in the middle of a verse (وسط الْآي) and those that appear at the end of a verse (رأس الْآي). They are further subdivided into those which are primary (aṣlī) and those which are additional (zāʾidah). Aṣlī would mean that they form part of the original word (part of the lām kalimah of the word), as apposed to zāʾidah; it is additional to the primary letters of the word.

Those which appear in the middle of verses total 36;[64] 13 are aṣlī and 23 are zāʾidah.[65] The number of yāʾ’s which appear at the end of verses are 87;6[6] five are aṣlī and 82 are zāʾidah.[67]

[62] This fifth difference is mentioned by Sheikh al-Ḍabbāʿ. See al-Iḍāʾah, pg. 56.

[63] Ibn al-Jazarī tallys the number of yāʾāt al-zawāʾid at 121, excluding فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِيِ عَنْ شَيْءٍ of Sūrat al-Kahf, 70, because the yāʾ is written in the maṣāḥif and therefore not included amongst the yāʾāt al-zawāʾid. If the yāʾ of فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِيِ is added, then the total will be 122, according to Ibn al-Jazarī’s count. See Al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pg. 182.

[64] Ibn al-Jazarī’s count is 35. See al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pg. 180.

[65] Though Ibn al-Jazarī totals the zāʾidah which comes in the middle of the verse as 22, Sheikh ʿAli al- Ḍabbāʾ adds يُرْدْنِ الرَّحْمٰنِ of Sūrah Yāsīn. Thus, the total will be 23 in the category which appears in the middle of the verse as zāʾidah. The overall total in this category will therefore be 36 and not 35 as tallied by Ibn al-Jazarī. And Allah knows best. See al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pp. 180-181, al-Iḍāʾah, pg. 55.

[67] Though Ibn al-Jazarī lists 81 in the category of zāʾidah at the end of the verse, he omits فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ of Sūrat al-Zumar, 17, which he includes in the category of zāʾidah which comes in the middle of the verse. See al-Nashr, Vol. 2, pp. 180-181.

And Abū Jaʿfar (makes ithbāṭ) during waṣl… In conformity with that which is (mentioned) in al-Ḥirz in الَّدَاعِ, وَاتَّقُونِ, تَسْأَلْنِ, تُؤْتُونِي, similarly in وَاخْشَوْنِ with لَا.

# Commentary

فِي الْحَالَيْنِ (in both conditions) in the verse refers to the conditions of waqf and waṣl

Yaʿqūb will have ithbāt of the yāʾ during waṣl and waqf of the yāʾ’s mentioned in the table above, whether they come in the middle of a verse or at the end of the verse (كَرُوسِ الآَيِ).

From this general application, مَنْ يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام is excluded.[71]

Thereafter the author discusses the practice of Abū Jaʿfar. In addition to him agreeing with his basis, he will also make ithbāt of the yāʾ during waṣl (مُوصِلَا) in 13 words, in conformity with Yaʿqūb, based upon what is mentioned in al-Ḥirz (يُوَافِقُ مَا فِيِ الْحْرْزِ) i.e. the Shāṭibiyyah. This means that Abū Jaʿfar will additionally make ithbāt during waṣl in 13 words (that comes in 14 places) in which Yaʿqūb agrees with his basis, Abū ʿAmr, as mentioned in the Shāṭibiyyah. Five of these words are mentioned in line 57:

1) الَّدَاعِ إِذَا – Sūrat al-Baqarah, 186.

2) وَاتَّقُونِ يَا أُولِي – Sūrat al-Baqarah, 197.

3) فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِ مَا – Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام, 46.

4) حَتّٰى تُؤْتُونِ مَوْثِقًا – Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, 66.

5) وَاخْشَوْنِ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا – Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 44.

The author adds the clause ‚مَعْ لَا‛ (with لَا) to specify this place and exclude other places like وَاخْشَوْنِ وَلِأْتِمّ of Sūrat al-Baqarah, 150 and وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah, 3.

Another seven places are mentioned in the next line.

[71] يَرْتَعْ of Sūrah Yūsuf will also be exluded because Yaʿqūb reads the ʿāyn as sākin i.e. يَرْتَعْ. One may also exclude فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ * الَّذِّينَ of Sūrat al-Zumar, 17; though Yaʿqūb will make ithbāt of the yāʾ during waqf; during waṣl it will be dropped due to ijtimāʾ al-sākinayn (two sākin letters meeting).
(Make ithbāt of the yāʾ for Abū Jaʿfar in) أَشْرَكْتُمُونِ, الْبَادِ, تُخْزُونِ, قَدْ هَدَانِ, اتَّبِعُونِ and then كِيدُونِ during waṣl.

# Commentary

The seven words mentioned in this verse are:

6) بِمَا أَشْرَكْتُمُونِي مِنْ قَبْلُ – Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, 22.

7) فِيهِ وَالْبَادِ – Sūrat al-Ḥajj, 25.

8) وَلَا تُخْزُونِ فِي ضَيْفِي – Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام, 78.

9) وَقَدْ هَدَانِ – Sūrat al-Anʿām, 80.

10) وَاتَّبِعُونِ هٰذَا – Sūrat al-Zukhruf, 61.

11) يٰقَوْمِ اتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُم – Sūrah Ghāfir, 38.

The place in Sūrah Ghāfir is included because it is encompassed by وَاتَّبِعُونِي which is mentioned generally in the line.

12) ثُمّ كِيدُونِ – Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, 195.

وُصِّلَا indicates that ithbāt will be made during waṣl.
(Make ithbāt of the yāʾ for Abū Jaʿfar in) دَعَانِ and وَخَافُونِ; make ithbāt in يُرِدْنِ and تَتَّبِعَنْ during both conditions for Abū Jaʿfar, adding a fatḥah (during waṣl).

# Commentary

The last two places are mentioned in this line:

13) إِذَا دَعَانِ – Sūrat al-Baqarah, 186.

14) وَخَافُونِ – Sūrah Āli ʿImrān, 175.

Besides these places, after Abū Jaʿfar makes ithbāt of the yāʾ during waqf and waṣl (بِحَالَيْهِ), he additionally (زَادَ) reads a fatḥah on the yāʾ during waṣl in:

1) يُرِدْنِ الرَّحْمٰنِ – Sūrah Yāsīn, 23.

2) أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنْ أَفَعَصَيْتَ – Sūrah Ṭāhā, 93.

Yaʿqūb makes ithbāt of the yāʾ during waqf in Sūrah Yāsin, and ḥadhf during waṣl; while making ithbāt of the yāʾ during waqf and waṣl in Sūrah Ṭāhā. Abū Jaʿfar will also make ithbāt during waqf and waṣl (بِحَالَيْهِ): as maftūḥah during waṣl and sākinah during waqf.

(Make ithbāt during waṣl) in تَلَاقِ and التَّنَادِي for Ibn Wardān; (make ithbāt during waqf and waṣl) in (يٰعِبَادِ فَاتَّقُونِ) عِبَادِي اتَّقُو for Ruways; (ithbāt during waṣl) in دُعآءِ for Abū Jaʿfar. Make ḥadhf (in the latter i.e. دُعآءِ) along with تُمِدُّونَنِيِ for Khalaf.

# Commentary

Ibn Wardān will make ithbāt of the yāʾ during waṣl in لِيُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ التَّلَاقِ and أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُم يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ of Sūrah Ghāfir, 15, 31 (تَلَاقِ التَّنَادِي بِنْ). During waqf he will drop the yāʾ. Ibn Jammāz will drop the yāʾ during waqf and waṣl.

عِبَادِي اتَّقُو refers to يٰعِبَادِ فَاتَّقُونِ of Sūrat al-Zumar, 16; Ruways makes ithbāt of the yāʾ during waqf and waṣl (عِبَادِي اتَّقُو طُمَا). Rouḥ has ḥadhf during waqf and waṣl.

Abū Jaʿfar will agree with his basis and read with ḥadhf.

In رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعآءِ of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, Abū Jaʿfar will differ with Qālūn and make ithbāt of the yāʾ during waṣl (دُعَاءِ اتْلُ).

Khalaf will differ with his basis and make ḥadhf of the yāʾ in دُعآءِ, as well as in أَتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمَالٍ of Sūrat al-Naml (وَاحْذِفْ مَعْ تُمِدُّونَنِيِ فُلَا).
(Make ḥadhf) in آتَانِ of (Sūrat) al-Naml for Rouḥ during waṣl. The consistent rules (uṣūl for the Qurrāʾ) are completed with the assistance of Allah, being like clear pearls.

# Commentary

In فَمَا آتَانِيَ اللُه خَيْرْ of Sūrat al-Naml, Rouḥ will make ḥadhf during waṣl (وَآتَانِ نَمْلٍ يُسْرْ). During waqf he will have ithbāt of the yāʾ. Ruways will agree with his basis and read the yāʾ as maftūḥah during waṣl and as sākinah during waqf.

Abū Jaʿfar will agree with his basis and read the yāʾ as maftūḥah during waṣl and drop it during waqf.

The uṣūl (rules) for the Three Qurrāʾ as completed, only through the will and assistance of Allah. These rules are explained in such a manner being as lucid as clear pearls.
